theme: Stephen’s sermon and martyrdom; Saul appears
readingInstruction: Read Acts 6:8-8:3. Stephen, one of the seven, is full of grace and power. He is arrested, gives a long speech to the council, and is stoned. A young man named Saul is introduced. Read Stephen’s last words slowly.
settingTheScene: Stephen, who was chosen to serve tables, also does signs and speaks with wisdom. Members of a synagogue argue with him and cannot withstand the Spirit by whom he spoke. They bring false witnesses who say he spoke against the temple and the law. His speech summarizes Israel’s history from Abraham to Solomon and ends with an accusation. His death begins a persecution that scatters the church and sets the stage for the gospel’s spread.
observation: “And Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people” (6:8).
“And gazing at him, all who sat in the council saw that his face was like the face of an angel” (6:15).
“The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia” (7:2).
“You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit” (7:51).
“But he, full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God” (7:55).
“Lord, do not hold this sin against them” (7:60).
“And there arose on that day a great persecution against the church in Jerusalem” (8:1).
interpretation:
Stephen is accused of speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God. He is brought before the council, and his face looks like an angel’s. When the high priest asks if these things are so, Stephen gives a long speech. It is not a defense but a sermon, retelling the history of Israel. His point is that God has never been confined to one place. The God of glory appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia, before there was a land or a temple. He was with Joseph in Egypt, with Moses in Midian and at Sinai. The tabernacle was a tent that moved, and Solomon built the temple, “yet the Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands.” At each stage, Israel resisted: Joseph’s brothers sold him, Israel rejected Moses, and they made a golden calf.

Then he turns the history on his hearers. “You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers did, so do you. Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, whom you have now betrayed and murdered.” They are enraged.

Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looks into heaven and sees the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. Everywhere else in the New Testament, Jesus is seated at the Father’s right hand. Here he stands, as if rising to receive his first martyr or to testify on his behalf. The crowd covers their ears, rushes him, drags him out of the city, and stones him. The witnesses lay their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.

Stephen’s death echoes Jesus’ death. He prays, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit,” and “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” He kneels and dies, and Luke says he “fell asleep.” Saul approved of his execution. A great persecution arises, and the church is scattered throughout Judea and Samaria, except the apostles. Saul ravages the church, entering house after house. But as Jesus said in Acts 1:8, the gospel is about to move beyond Jerusalem. The scattering of the church is the way the word of God spreads.
connection: Genesis 12 to 50, Exodus, and 1 Kings 6 and 8 are the history Stephen retells. Isaiah 66:1-2 is quoted in the speech. Jeremiah 7:1-15 warned about trusting in the temple. Deuteronomy 10:16 and Jeremiah 9:26 speak of uncircumcised hearts. Luke 23:34 and 23:46 are Jesus’ similar prayers. Matthew 5:10-12 blesses the persecuted. Philippians 1:29 says we are given the privilege of suffering for his sake. Acts 22:20 has Paul recalling Stephen’s death.
application:
Notice how Stephen was able to forgive. Pray for someone who has harmed you.

Ask what “houses made by hands” you trust in: a building, a tradition, a routine? Remember that God goes with his people.

Pray for Christians who are persecuted today by name if you know them.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to fill you with the Holy Spirit.
Ask him for courage, like Stephen’s, to look to heaven.
Pray for those who oppose you, as Stephen did.
